meta.source: The Koerner Office podcast, 384-episode catalog, indexed 2026-07
meta.note: Idea summaries in FILG's own words. Economics carry a label: what the number is and who claims it. Episode counts are the catalog's demand signal, shown as-is.

ideas.title: AI Assessment Agency
ideas.one_liner: Run structured AI-readiness interviews with small business owners, deliver a formatted tool-recommendation report in 48 hours, upsell the implementation work.
ideas.startup_cost: near zero (Retell.ai, Claude, Gamma free tiers)

economics.claim: $1,000 per assessment, grown from free to $200 to $500
economics.label: named operator, verified on screen
economics.note: Corey shows the actual report on camera; $1,000 price point is current but recent

ideas.method: 20-45 minute discovery interview (Zoom or an AI voice agent), feed the transcript to Claude to map pain points to off-the-shelf tools, deliver an effort-vs-impact report within 48 hours.

ideas.title: No-Code Micro SaaS
ideas.one_liner: Find a niche problem people complain about, validate demand with keyword research, build the MVP with vibe-coding tools, sell monthly subscriptions.
ideas.startup_cost: $0-200/mo (Claude Code or Bolt, Supabase and Vercel free tiers)

economics.claim: $5K MRR in first full month, 267 paying users, three tiers, 80-85% margins
economics.label: named operator, self-reported
economics.note: Vadim's numbers are internally consistent and corroborated in the interview

economics.claim: $3M/year ARR across 24 micro-SaaS tools
economics.label: named operator, self-reported
economics.note: John Rush; portfolio-level, not one product

ideas.method: Validate the complaint before building: Reddit and X complaints plus Google autocomplete and keyword volume. Then Bolt or Lovable for UI, Supabase for data, Claude Code for iteration.

ideas.title: Cold Email Agency
ideas.one_liner: Done-for-you B2B outreach: build the prospect list, manage deliverability infrastructure, write 3-line sequences, book meetings on a monthly retainer.

economics.claim: 60 clients at $1,500/mo, described as almost all profit
economics.label: named operator, self-reported
economics.note: podcast-booking niche agency; margins not audited, fulfillment cost undisclosed

ideas.method: Pick a hyper-specific ICP, build a verified list, warm 10-50 domains for 21 days, send short plain-text sequences, charge a retainer for booked meetings.

ideas.title: Facebook Ads Agency for Local Services
ideas.one_liner: Run Meta ad campaigns for high-LTV local service businesses (tree trimming, HVAC, cleaning) on a flat monthly retainer.

economics.claim: tree trimming: $5 leads at $15/day budget, 4 jobs in week one
economics.label: named operator, verified on screen
economics.note: the host's own tested campaign; small sample

economics.claim: roofing leads at $20 each in Louisiana
economics.label: named operator, self-reported
economics.note: instructor's client, corroborates the range

ideas.method: Learn Meta Ads Manager, build 3-5 free case studies with real iPhone photos, then charge retainers. Message objective plus before/after photos for home services.

ideas.title: Claude Skill / Prompt Selling
ideas.one_liner: Package real domain expertise into Claude skill files, bundle 20-25 of them at $99, sell via a landing page with Stripe and content marketing.
ideas.startup_cost: under $100 (domain, Stripe, hosting); time-heavy to build the stack

economics.claim: $3,000+ in about 40 days from a 25-skill bundle plus one $1,000 consulting upsell
economics.label: named operator, verified on screen
economics.note: Ryan Dozer showed the Stripe dashboard live; one data point from someone with existing SEO clients

ideas.method: Pick a domain you actually know, structure the knowledge into skill markdown with Claude's skill creator, build a simple landing page, price the bundle at $99.

ideas.title: AI Automation Agency
ideas.one_liner: Audit small companies for AI use cases, then build or install the automations: from ChatGPT workflow coaching to custom agentic apps on a fractional basis.
ideas.startup_cost: near zero (tools you already use: Claude, Zapier, n8n, Make)

economics.claim: roughly $800K annual run rate at month 5, from $4-5K one-time projects
economics.label: named operator, self-reported
economics.note: Brandon's own figures; the discovery methodology and pricing ladder ($10-15K audit, $20-35K/mo fractional) are the useful part

ideas.method: Discovery call to map workflows, classify fixes into education / off-the-shelf integrations / custom builds, ship 3-5 working prototypes in the first 30 days, report time and cost saved.

ideas.title: AI UGC Ad Agency
ideas.one_liner: Create AI-generated UGC-style video ads and sell them to companies already spending heavily on Meta ads, found via the public Ads Library.

economics.claim: $0 to $10-20M ARR app cited as a client result
economics.label: flagged not credible
economics.note: the claim comes from the Arcads founder promoting his own tool; no third-party verification

economics.claim: $2K/month per client; 10 clients = $20K/mo
economics.label: host estimate or hypothetical
economics.note: the mechanic (find 50+ active ads, offer a free sample, land a retainer) is concrete; the revenue math is illustrative

ideas.method: Find brands with 50+ active ads in the Facebook Ads Library, make a free AI sample ad, cold-outreach the CEO on LinkedIn, convert to a monthly retainer.

ideas.title: Amazon KDP Low-Content Books
ideas.one_liner: Publish AI-assisted journals, planners and puzzle books on Amazon KDP with zero inventory, picking niches via BookBolt keyword gaps.

economics.claim: $500K/mo from two books
economics.label: flagged not credible
economics.note: no verifiable operator; the number came from a ChatGPT research output

economics.claim: $1K/month per winning book
economics.label: host estimate or hypothetical
economics.note: clean hypothetical math, not an observed case

ideas.method: BookBolt for search-volume-vs-competition gaps, templates plus AI for interiors and covers, optimize the title structure, publish free on KDP. Thin moat; volume game.

ideas.title: Etsy Print-on-Demand at Scale
ideas.one_liner: Reverse-engineer Etsy bestsellers, generate derivative graphics with the ChatGPT image API, list through Printify via n8n automation, target 10,000+ listings.
ideas.startup_cost: $40-60/mo (Everbe, ChatGPT, n8n; Printify pays per order)

economics.claim: another $100K/year is not unreasonable with this strategy
economics.label: named operator, self-reported
economics.note: Cody has run POD for 10+ years; stated belief, not a current P&L

ideas.method: Everbe to find winners, image API for derivative designs, background removal, Printify sync via n8n, iterate toward the listings that stick.

ideas.title: Etsy Digital Printables
ideas.one_liner: Find Etsy's hidden bestseller list with the star-to-best URL hack, regenerate improved versions of proven printables, sell as instant downloads.
ideas.startup_cost: near zero (Picsart free tier, $0.20 per listing)

economics.claim: one store: 87,000 reviews, extrapolated to millions in lifetime sales
economics.label: host estimate or hypothetical
economics.note: review counts are real on-screen data; the revenue extrapolation is the host's back-of-envelope

ideas.method: Search printables, filter Star Sellers, swap star for best in the URL, find high sales-per-SKU sellers, make a better derivative, match their keywords. IP and ToS exposure is the risk.

ideas.title: Productized Design Subscription
ideas.one_liner: Productize one digital skill (design, copy, video editing) as a flat monthly subscription: a site, a price, a subscribe button, no calls, no proposals.

economics.claim: DesignJoy: $1M/year revenue, $70-80K/mo net solo, started at $449/mo
economics.label: named operator, verified on screen
economics.note: Brett Williams; DesignJoy is a verifiable public company and the model's canonical case

ideas.method: Pick the skill, build a one-page site with the price and a subscribe button, launch on Product Hunt, start cheap and raise until churn says stop.

ideas.title: Government Contract Brokering
ideas.one_liner: Register an LLC on sam.gov, bid on sub-$350K service contracts with subcontractor quotes plus a markup, manage the sub while collecting the spread.

economics.claim: $10-12K/month steady-state; one $962K 5-year contract netted $262K
economics.label: named operator, self-reported
economics.note: Natalie, on camera with granular unit economics; internally consistent

ideas.method: Browse sam.gov for under-$350K contracts (no past-performance requirement), parse solicitations with AI, quote 2-3 subs, bid with a markup. Legal caveat: stay under the 50% self-performance rule; a PTAC consult is the cheap gate.

ideas.title: Rank-and-Rent Local Lead Gen
ideas.one_liner: Build local service websites that rank in Google organic and Maps, then rent the leads to one local business per site for a flat monthly fee.
ideas.startup_cost: under $500 for the first 3 sites (hosting, tracking numbers, keyword tools)

economics.claim: one carpet-cleaning site: #1 for years, $500/mo flat, roughly $50K lifetime on $10/mo hosting
economics.label: named operator, verified on screen
economics.note: Luke; the site and ranking were shown live

economics.claim: $100K/month company-level, $35K/month personal
economics.label: named operator, self-reported
economics.note: Kyle; dashboard shown, company figure is partnership-level

ideas.method: Exact-match domain, thin but real local site, Google Business Profile on a tracking number, target 60-300K population cities, sell the leads to businesses already buying Google Ads.

ideas.title: Niche Directory Websites
ideas.one_liner: Build consumer directory sites for underserved local searches (thrift stores, Medicaid-accepting therapists), monetize with display ads and featured listings.
ideas.startup_cost: $100-300 (domain, hosting, a directory plugin, keyword tool trial)

economics.claim: 3 directory sites, $2,300-3,000/month combined, untouched for 6 months
economics.label: named operator, verified on screen
economics.note: traffic graph visible on screen; revenue stated verbatim

ideas.method: Find demand with the near-me keyword method past page 5, the inurl:directory hack, and Reddit 'looking for' mining; build around an underserved filter; rank and collect.

ideas.title: Credit Card Points Consulting
ideas.one_liner: Charge business owners a flat fee to optimize their card strategy and points, plus a separate fee to book award travel with what they earn.

economics.claim: $231K gross in the first full year, about $40K expenses
economics.label: named operator, self-reported
economics.note: Colin Stroud, on camera with expense breakdown; a personal-brand business that took 15+ months of daily LinkedIn posting to ramp

ideas.method: Learn the rewards landscape from free sources, post deal finds on LinkedIn 1-2x daily, sell an $875 audit package plus a trip-booking service.

ideas.title: Missed-Call AI Receptionist Service
ideas.one_liner: Install an AI text-back agent on a local business's phone line so missed calls become qualified, booked appointments; charge a monthly retainer.
ideas.startup_cost: $100-300/mo (GoHighLevel; scraping and voicemail-drop tools per use)

economics.claim: $500-2,000/month per client
economics.label: host estimate or hypothetical
economics.note: the live demo works (real callback engaged the bot) but no paying client is shown; saturated GHL-reseller pitch, margins compress

ideas.method: GoHighLevel workflow: missed-call trigger, AI conversation prompt per business type, booked/emergency/unqualified branches. Duplicate per client.

ideas.title: AI Pitch Deck Service
ideas.one_liner: Generate draft pitch decks from public SEC filings with AI, send the first 5 slides watermarked as outreach, charge $3,500 for the full deck.
ideas.startup_cost: $20-70/mo (Manus via Perplexity Pro, Apollo for leads)

economics.claim: $3,500 per deck
economics.label: named operator, self-reported
economics.note: the 'pitch deck guy on Twitter' is a real practitioner comp; the fully automated version is speculative

ideas.method: Scrape new fund filings, auto-generate a draft deck, cold-send the teaser, deliver the premium version manually.

ideas.title: Niche Job Board
ideas.one_liner: Run a narrowly targeted job board (by profession or identity) on off-the-shelf software, aggregate supply via APIs, charge employers for posts.

economics.claim: a physician job board doing $80M/year
economics.label: flagged not credible
economics.note: asserted by the host with no name or source; disregard the number, keep the structural model

ideas.method: Pick a defensible niche where the audience congregates, spin up the board no-code, seed supply by aggregating, monetize employer posts. The niche angle is unvalidated.

ideas.title: Faceless AI YouTube Channel
ideas.one_liner: High-CPM niche long-form videos produced end-to-end with AI (script, cinematic clips, thumbnails); monetize AdSense, affiliates, or the channel sale.

economics.claim: $5-30K/month from faceless channels; finance RPM $15-30 per 1K views
economics.label: host estimate or hypothetical
economics.note: workflow demonstrated live, zero channel revenue shown; RPM ranges are industry-common figures

ideas.method: Pick dark-business-history or similar high-CPM niche, one prompt for titles and script, generate 12 cinematic shots, assemble, publish on a cadence. Months to payoff, algorithm risk.

ideas.title: Multilingual Voicemail Service for Realtors
ideas.one_liner: Clone a realtor's voice, generate their standard voicemails in 4+ languages, sell as a setup fee plus monthly retainer in multilingual markets.

economics.claim: $300-500/month per realtor; 10 realtors = $3K/mo
economics.label: host estimate or hypothetical
economics.note: live demo works (17-second clone); no paying clients shown; realtor churn is high

ideas.method: Clone from their public video, translate 10 standard scripts with an LLM, render in their voice, pitch by sending them their own cloned sample.

ideas.title: Google Ads Agency for Local Services
ideas.one_liner: Run Google Search and YouTube campaigns for local services, with landing-page conversion as the differentiator.

economics.claim: cleaning businesses: $60 to close a $300-500/mo recurring customer
economics.label: named operator, self-reported
economics.note: an instructor's real students, specific but unnamed

ideas.method: Target high-LTV local services, do 2-3 free campaigns for testimonials, win on the landing page, then charge.

ideas.title: Domain Name Investing
ideas.one_liner: Buy expiring or undervalued .com domains at auction; flip them, or build a niche directory on an aged exact-match name.
ideas.startup_cost: $5 per closeout domain to $17K+ for premium names

economics.claim: DudeRanch.com: $50K/year from about an hour a month, after 14 years
economics.label: named operator, self-reported
economics.note: the owner's direct disclosure with advertiser count and flat fee; note the 14-year ramp

ideas.method: Monitor expiring auctions filtered by age, length and .com; value by exact-match search volume and backlinks; flip or build.

ideas.title: Paid Niche Community
ideas.one_liner: Build a paid community around a real expertise, using abandoned Meetup groups as a near-free member acquisition hack.

economics.claim: top 50 Skool groups average $53K MRR; the biggest is $555K MRR
economics.label: host estimate or hypothetical
economics.note: the host's own scrape of public Skool data; member counts and prices are public, the average is his calculation

ideas.method: Join Meetups in your niche, take over groups when organizers step down, co-host events, funnel members into a paid community.
